```{r setup}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(qs2)
library(here)
library(scales)
library(stringr)

# --- No sourcing of data-sim07-all.R ----------------------------------------
# Unlike the sim09 report, this report does NOT source the simulation script.
# data-sim07-all.R compiles the Stan model, initialises a log file and parses
# command-line arguments at source time, and it has no summary functions that
# match the sim09 ones. Everything needed is computed here, directly from the
# results files written by sim07_sim_loop() (cfg, d_decision, d_all), so
# data-sim07-all.R is left untouched.

# --- plain-language labels, reused throughout (identical to sim09 report) ---
domain_labs <- c(
  d1 = "D1: Surgical strategy\n(DAIR vs revision)",
  d2 = "D2: Antibiotic duration\n(12wk vs 6wk, after 1-stage revision)",
  d3 = "D3: Extended prophylaxis\n(12wk vs none, after 2-stage revision)",
  d4 = "D4: Rifampicin\n(added vs not)"
)
rule_labs <- c(sup = "Superiority", ni = "Non-inferiority", fut = "Futility")

wrap_lab <- function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 28)
```

```{r sim07-helpers}
# =============================================================================
# sim07 equivalents of the sim09 summary functions
# =============================================================================

# sim07 coding (see get_sim07_trial_data):
#   s  : 1 = early, 2 = late-acute (randomised to d1), 3 = chronic
#   d1 : 1 = dair, 2 = one-stage revision (pref 1), 3 = two-stage (pref 2)
#   d2 : 1 = not entered, 2 = 12wk, 3 = 6wk        (NA unless d1 == 2)
#   d3 : 1 = not entered, 2 = none, 3 = 12wk       (NA unless d1 == 3)
#   d4 : 1 = not entered, 2 = no rif, 3 = rif
# Contrasts (from the Stan generated quantities): rd_d1 = rev - dair,
# rd_d2 = 6wk - 12wk, rd_d3 = 12wk - none, rd_d4 = rif - none.

# Map sim07 decision types onto the sim09 rule labels. 'prec' gives the
# precedence when two rules for the same domain first trigger at the same
# interim; superiority/ni wins, matching the if/else order in
# get_sim07_trial_data (which is what actually governed allocation).
sim07_rule_map <- data.table(
  domain = c("d1", "d1", "d2", "d2", "d3", "d3", "d4", "d4"),
  quant  = c("sup", "fut_sup", "ni", "fut_ni", "sup", "fut_sup", "sup", "fut_sup"),
  rule   = c("sup", "fut", "ni", "fut", "sup", "fut", "sup", "fut"),
  prec   = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2)
)

# First (locking) decision per simulated trial and domain.
# sim07 locks each decision type separately (cumsum per type), so a domain can
# later flag a second, contradictory rule (e.g. superiority at interim 2 then
# futility at interim 4). Only the first decision changed allocation in
# sim07, so only the first is counted - which is how sim09 defines it too.
sim07_first_dec <- function(d_decision) {
  d <- melt(
    copy(d_decision), id.vars = c("sim", "ia", "quant"),
    measure.vars = paste0("d", 1:4),
    variable.name = "domain", value.name = "dec")
  d[, `:=`(domain = as.character(domain),
           sim = as.integer(sim), ia = as.integer(ia),
           dec = as.logical(dec))]
  d <- merge(d, sim07_rule_map, by = c("domain", "quant"))
  d <- d[dec == TRUE]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(data.table())
  setorder(d, sim, domain, ia, prec)
  d <- d[, .SD[1], by = .(sim, domain)]
  d[, .(i_sim = sim, domain, i_anlys = ia, rule)]
}

# Cumulative chance of each (first) decision by interim - sim09_smry_pr_dec
sim07_smry_pr_dec <- function(d_decision, n_interim) {
  sims <- sort(unique(as.integer(d_decision$sim)))
  d_first <- sim07_first_dec(d_decision)

  d_grid <- CJ(i_sim = sims, i_anlys = seq_len(n_interim),
               domain = paste0("d", 1:4))
  d_grid <- merge(unique(sim07_rule_map[, .(domain, rule)]), d_grid,
                  by = "domain", allow.cartesian = TRUE)

  if (nrow(d_first) > 0) {
    setnames(d_first, c("i_anlys", "rule"), c("first_ia", "first_rule"))
    d_grid <- merge(d_grid, d_first, by = c("i_sim", "domain"), all.x = TRUE)
  } else {
    d_grid[, `:=`(first_ia = NA_integer_, first_rule = NA_character_)]
  }
  d_grid[, dec01 := as.numeric(!is.na(first_ia) & rule == first_rule &
                                 i_anlys >= first_ia)]

  d_out <- d_grid[, .(mu = mean(dec01)), keyby = .(i_anlys, domain, rule)]
  d_out[, rule := factor(rule, levels = c("sup", "ni", "fut"))]
  setorder(d_out, domain, rule)
  d_out
}

# Cumulative enrolment, and the number informing each domain's own contrast,
# by simulated trial and interim (same definitions as sim09_domain_n):
#   d1: all late-acute (randomised) patients
#   d2: one-stage revision patients randomised to 12wk or 6wk (all silos)
#   d3: two-stage revision patients randomised to 12wk or none (all silos)
#   d4: patients randomised to rif or no rif (all silos)
sim07_cum_n <- function(d_all) {
  d <- copy(d_all)
  to_int <- function(x) as.integer(as.character(x))
  d[, `:=`(sim = as.integer(sim), ia = as.integer(ia),
           s = to_int(s), d1 = to_int(d1), d2 = to_int(d2),
           d3 = to_int(d3), d4 = to_int(d4))]
  d_n <- d[, .(
    n_enrolled = sum(N),
    d1 = sum(N[s == 2]),
    d2 = sum(N[d1 == 2 & d2 %in% 2:3]),
    d3 = sum(N[d1 == 3 & d3 %in% 2:3]),
    d4 = sum(N[d4 %in% 2:3])
  ), keyby = .(sim, ia)]
  cols <- c("n_enrolled", paste0("d", 1:4))
  d_n[, (cols) := lapply(.SD, function(z) cumsum(as.double(z))),
      by = sim, .SDcols = cols]
  melt(d_n, id.vars = c("sim", "ia", "n_enrolled"),
       variable.name = "domain", value.name = "n_inform",
       variable.factor = FALSE)
}

# Patients enrolled / informing at the first decision - sim09_smry_dec_info
sim07_smry_dec_info <- function(d_decision, d_all) {
  n_sim <- uniqueN(d_decision$sim)
  d_first <- sim07_first_dec(d_decision)
  if (nrow(d_first) == 0 || is.null(d_all)) {
    return(list(d_inform_tot = data.table(), d_smry = data.table()))
  }
  d_n <- sim07_cum_n(d_all)
  d_inform <- merge(
    d_first, d_n,
    by.x = c("i_sim", "i_anlys", "domain"), by.y = c("sim", "ia", "domain"),
    all.x = TRUE)
  d_inform[, inform_prop := n_inform / n_enrolled]

  d_summary <- d_inform[, .(
    n_dec = .N,
    pr_dec = .N / n_sim,
    mu_n_enrl = mean(n_enrolled),
    q025_n_enrl = quantile(n_enrolled, 0.025),
    q975_n_enrl = quantile(n_enrolled, 0.975),
    mu_n_info = mean(n_inform),
    q025_n_info = quantile(n_inform, 0.025),
    q975_n_info = quantile(n_inform, 0.975),
    prop_info = mean(inform_prop)
  ), keyby = .(domain, rule)]
  d_summary[, rule := factor(rule, levels = c("sup", "ni", "fut"))]
  setorder(d_summary, domain, rule)

  list(d_inform_tot = d_inform, d_smry = d_summary)
}

# True standardised risk differences implied by the sim07 data-generating
# process, for the estimands defined in the sim07 Stan generated quantities,
# evaluated in the design population (all domains open, i.e. before any
# adaptation changes allocation). This mirrors sim09_true_effects_des_pop.
#   d1: late silo. DAIR over everyone at their own preference and d4.
#       Revision = one-stage (d2 held at 'not entered') for preference-1
#       patients, two-stage (d3 held at 'not entered') for preference-2,
#       mixed by the preference proportions.
#   d2: all one-stage patients (all silos), 6wk vs 12wk.
#   d3: all two-stage patients (all silos), 12wk vs none.
#   d4: patients entering d4 (all silos), rif vs none.
sim07_true_effects <- function(cfg) {

  mu <- cfg$mu
  bs <- unlist(cfg$bs)
  bp <- unlist(cfg$bp)
  bd1 <- c(unlist(cfg$l_e$bd1), unlist(cfg$l_l$bd1), unlist(cfg$l_c$bd1))
  bd2 <- unlist(cfg$bd2); bd3 <- unlist(cfg$bd3); bd4 <- unlist(cfg$bd4)
  p_s <- unlist(cfg$p_s_alloc)
  l_s <- list(cfg$l_e, cfg$l_l, cfg$l_c)

  p_lvl <- function(entry, alloc) c(1 - entry, entry * (1 - alloc), entry * alloc)
  p_d4 <- function(s) p_lvl(l_s[[s]]$p_d4_entry, l_s[[s]]$p_d4_alloc)
  p_d2 <- function(s) p_lvl(l_s[[s]]$p_d2_entry, l_s[[s]]$p_d2_alloc)
  p_d3 <- function(s) p_lvl(l_s[[s]]$p_d3_entry, l_s[[s]]$p_d3_alloc)

  # linear predictor exactly as in get_sim07_trial_data
  eta <- function(s, pref, d1, d2 = 1, d3 = 1, d4) {
    ix <- d1 + 3 * (s - 1)
    if (d1 == 1) mu + bs[s] + bp[pref] + bd1[ix] + bd4[d4]
    else if (d1 == 2) mu + bs[s] + bd1[ix] + bd2[d2] + bd4[d4]
    else mu + bs[s] + bp[pref] + bd1[ix] + bd3[d3] + bd4[d4]
  }
  # expected probability, averaging over d4 within silo s
  e_d4 <- function(s, f) sum(p_d4(s) * sapply(1:3, function(k) plogis(f(k))))

  # ---- d1 (late silo, s = 2) ----
  pp2 <- l_s[[2]]$p_pref
  p_dair <- (1 - pp2) * e_d4(2, function(k) eta(2, 1, 1, d4 = k)) +
    pp2 * e_d4(2, function(k) eta(2, 2, 1, d4 = k))
  p_r1 <- e_d4(2, function(k) eta(2, 1, 2, d2 = 1, d4 = k))
  p_r2 <- e_d4(2, function(k) eta(2, 2, 3, d3 = 1, d4 = k))
  p_rev <- (1 - pp2) * p_r1 + pp2 * p_r2

  # ---- d2 (one-stage patients, all silos) ----
  w2 <- sapply(1:3, function(s) p_s[s] * l_s[[s]]$p_d1_alloc * (1 - l_s[[s]]$p_pref))
  w2 <- w2 / sum(w2)
  p_d2_arm <- sapply(2:3, function(lvl) sum(w2 * sapply(1:3, function(s)
    e_d4(s, function(k) eta(s, 1, 2, d2 = lvl, d4 = k)))))

  # ---- d3 (two-stage patients, all silos) ----
  w3 <- sapply(1:3, function(s) p_s[s] * l_s[[s]]$p_d1_alloc * l_s[[s]]$p_pref)
  w3 <- w3 / sum(w3)
  p_d3_arm <- sapply(2:3, function(lvl) sum(w3 * sapply(1:3, function(s)
    e_d4(s, function(k) eta(s, 2, 3, d3 = lvl, d4 = k)))))

  # ---- d4 (d4 entrants, all silos) ----
  w4 <- sapply(1:3, function(s) p_s[s] * l_s[[s]]$p_d4_entry)
  w4 <- w4 / sum(w4)
  p_d4_arm <- sapply(2:3, function(lvl) {
    sum(w4 * sapply(1:3, function(s) {
      pa <- l_s[[s]]$p_d1_alloc; pp <- l_s[[s]]$p_pref
      dair <- (1 - pp) * plogis(eta(s, 1, 1, d4 = lvl)) +
        pp * plogis(eta(s, 2, 1, d4 = lvl))
      r1 <- sum(p_d2(s) * sapply(1:3, function(j) plogis(eta(s, 1, 2, d2 = j, d4 = lvl))))
      r2 <- sum(p_d3(s) * sapply(1:3, function(j) plogis(eta(s, 2, 3, d3 = j, d4 = lvl))))
      (1 - pa) * dair + pa * (1 - pp) * r1 + pa * pp * r2
    }))
  })

  data.table(
    domain = paste0("d", 1:4),
    p_ref = c(p_dair, p_d2_arm[1], p_d3_arm[1], p_d4_arm[1]),
    p_trt = c(p_rev, p_d2_arm[2], p_d3_arm[2], p_d4_arm[2])
  )[, `:=`(truth = p_trt - p_ref,
           truth_lor = qlogis(p_trt) - qlogis(p_ref))][]
}
```

# About this report

This report summarises the earlier **sim07** simulations in the same format as the sim09 report, so that the operating characteristics of the two approaches can be compared side by side.
Only the high-level summaries across scenarios are reproduced here; scenario-by-scenario detail and the appendix are not yet included.

ROADMAP is an adaptive platform trial in prosthetic joint infection.
It has four domains and is designed to stop recruiting into a domain when the accumulated evidence is strong enough but continue recruitment into the other domains.
Loosely, the four questions are:

- **D1 - Surgical strategy:** is revision surgery (removing and replacing the joint) better than DAIR (debridement and implant retention) for patients with a late-acute infection?
- **D2 - Antibiotic duration:** among patients having a one-stage revision (r1), is a shorter (6-week) course of antibiotics non-inferior to a 12-week course?
- **D3 - Extended prophylaxis:** among patients having a two-stage revision (r2), does an extra 12 weeks of preventive antibiotics improve outcomes compared with none?
- **D4 - Rifampicin:** does adding rifampicin to the antibiotic regimen improve outcomes?

At each interim analysis, the trial looks at the data collected to date for each of these four questions and asks whether the evidence is strong enough to draw a conclusion.
If so, the simulation stops randomising patients to that question and adopts the better (or, for d2, non-inferior) option going forward.
Futility stopping is also implemented.

```{r load-data}
f_list <- list.files(here::here("data", params$sim_dir), pattern = "\\.qs2$")

scenario_files <- lapply(f_list, function(f) {
  qs2::qs_read(here::here("data", params$sim_dir, f))
})

# scenario label: the cfg description where present, else the file name
scenario_names <- vapply(seq_along(scenario_files), function(i) {
  d <- scenario_files[[i]]$cfg$desc
  if (is.null(d) || !nzchar(d)) sub("\\.qs2$", "", f_list[i]) else d
}, character(1))
scenario_names <- make.unique(scenario_names, sep = " #")
names(scenario_files) <- scenario_names

n_sim_obs <- vapply(scenario_files, function(x) uniqueN(x$d_decision$sim), numeric(1))
```

This report covers `r length(scenario_files)` scenario(s):

```{r , results='asis'}
cat("\n")
for(scn in scenario_names){
  cat("\n+ ", scn, "\n")
}
```

The results data are those stored in **`r params$sim_dir`** and have **`r paste(unique(n_sim_obs), collapse = " / ")`** iterations per scenario.

# How to read the results

For each scenario, we report:

1. **Chance of reaching each decision, by interim** - across many simulated trials, what proportion concluded superiority / non-inferiority / futility for each domain, by each interim analysis.
2. **Typical patient numbers** - how many patients are typically enrolled, and how many directly inform each domain's own comparison, by the time a decision is reached.

These are defined exactly as in the sim09 report so the two can be read side by side.

# Simulation configuration

The table(s) below describe parts of the design that are the same across every scenario in this report; only the assumed true effects differ.

```{r config-tables}
cfg_list <- lapply(scenario_files, function(x) x$cfg)
chk <- function(f) length(unique(lapply(cfg_list, function(z) unlist(f(z))))) > 1
if (chk(function(z) z$p_s_alloc) || chk(function(z) z$thresh) ||
    chk(function(z) z$delta) || chk(function(z) z$N)) {
  warning("Silo proportions, enrolment schedule and/or decision rules differ across scenario files - the single 'simulation configuration' summary below no longer applies to all of them.")
}

cfg1 <- cfg_list[[1]]

domain_labs_short <- c(
  d1 = "D1: Surgical strategy", d2 = "D2: Antibiotic duration",
  d3 = "D3: Extended prophylaxis", d4 = "D4: Rifampicin"
)

table_silo_d1 <- function(cfg) {
  silo_labs <- c("Early infection", "Late-acute, randomised", "Chronic infection")
  l_s <- list(cfg$l_e, cfg$l_l, cfg$l_c)
  rbindlist(lapply(c(2, 1, 3), function(s) {
    pa <- l_s[[s]]$p_d1_alloc; pp <- l_s[[s]]$p_pref
    data.table(
      Silo = silo_labs[s],
      `Share of all patients` = percent(unname(cfg$p_s_alloc[s]), accuracy = 1),
      `D1 randomised?` = if (s == 2) "Yes" else "No (clinician choice)",
      `Preference for 2-stage` = percent(pp, accuracy = 1),
      DAIR = percent(1 - pa, accuracy = 1),
      `1-stage revision` = percent(pa * (1 - pp), accuracy = 1),
      `2-stage revision` = percent(pa * pp, accuracy = 1)
    )
  }))
}

# sim07 stores margins by rule type and thresholds by domain
table_decision_rules <- function(cfg) {
  spec <- data.table(
    domain = c("d1", "d1", "d2", "d2", "d3", "d3", "d4", "d4"),
    rule   = c("sup", "fut", "ni", "fut", "sup", "fut", "sup", "fut"),
    delta  = c("sup", "sup_fut", "ni", "ni_fut", "sup", "sup_fut", "sup", "sup_fut"),
    thresh = c("sup", "fut_sup", "ni", "fut_ni", "sup", "fut_sup", "sup", "fut_sup"),
    ix     = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4)
  )
  spec[, .(
    Domain = domain_labs_short[domain],
    Rule = rule_labs[rule],
    `Effect margin (delta)` = sprintf("%+.3f", mapply(function(d) cfg$delta[[d]], delta)),
    `Confidence required` = percent(
      mapply(function(t, i) unlist(cfg$thresh[[t]])[i], thresh, ix), accuracy = 0.1)
  )]
}
```

sim07 has three silos.
Only the late-acute silo is randomised to DAIR versus revision; early and chronic infections receive whichever surgical strategy their clinician deems appropriate.
Unlike sim09, there is no separate late-acute non-randomised group: all late-acute patients are assumed to enter the D1 randomisation.
The type of revision (one-stage vs two-stage) is set by the surgeon's preference, which is elicited at baseline before the randomisation is revealed.

```{r table-silo-d1, eval = F}
table_silo_d1(cfg1) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Patient population and initial surgical-strategy distribution") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 13)
```

## Analysis model

The sim07 analysis model is a single logistic regression with an intercept, silo effects, a preference effect, a 3x3 set of silo-by-surgery (d1) effects, and vector terms for d2, d3 and d4, where each includes a level for patients who did not enter the domain.
D2 terms enter only for one-stage patients and D3 terms only for two-stage patients.
The silo main effects and the silo-by-surgery terms overlap, so those parameters are separated only by their priors; the treatment contrasts are unaffected because they depend only on the sums.

Treatment effects are obtained by g-computation inside Stan, with standardisation weights drawn from a Bayesian bootstrap (Dirichlet weights on the observed covariate patterns) at each posterior draw.

- **D1** compares DAIR with revision in the late-acute silo. Revision is taken as one-stage for patients whose surgeon preferred one-stage and two-stage for those who preferred two-stage, with the downstream D2/D3 treatment held at the 'not entered' level. The two are combined in the observed preference proportions.
- **D2 and D3** standardise over all one-stage (respectively two-stage) patients across silos, including those who did not enter the domain.
- **D4** standardises over patients randomised within D4.

## Decision rules

For each domain, a decision is reached once the trial is sufficiently confident that the true effect exceeds (or, for futility, falls short of) a pre-specified margin.
In sim07 each rule is evaluated and locked separately, so a domain can trigger a second rule after its first.
Only the **first** decision changed allocation in sim07, so only the first is counted here, matching sim09.
Where two rules for a domain first trigger at the same interim, superiority (or non-inferiority) takes precedence, as in the sim07 allocation logic.

```{r table-decision-rules}
table_decision_rules(cfg1) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Domain") |>
  tab_header(title = "Decision rules by domain") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 13)
```

```{r compute-oc, results='hide'}
oc_by_scenario <- lapply(scenario_files, function(l) {
  cfg <- l$cfg
  list(
    cfg = cfg,
    dec_pr = sim07_smry_pr_dec(l$d_decision, length(cfg$N)),
    l_dec_info = sim07_smry_dec_info(l$d_decision, l$d_all),
    truth = sim07_true_effects(cfg)
  )
})
```

```{r overall-fns}
rule_cols <- c(Superiority = "#2C7FB8", `Non-inferiority` = "#31A354", Futility = "#D95F0E")

scn_factor <- function(x, width = 28) {
  factor(str_wrap(x, width), levels = str_wrap(scenario_names, width))
}

# stack one element of every scenario's summary into a single table
stack_oc <- function(get_fn) {
  rbindlist(lapply(scenario_names, function(scn) {
    d <- get_fn(oc_by_scenario[[scn]])
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
    d <- copy(d)
    d[, scenario := scn]
    d
  }), fill = TRUE)
}

d_dec_all   <- stack_oc(function(oc) oc$dec_pr)
d_info_all  <- stack_oc(function(oc) oc$l_dec_info$d_smry)
d_truth_all <- stack_oc(function(oc) oc$truth[, .(domain, truth, truth_lor, p_ref, p_trt)])

d_dec_all[, rule_lab := factor(rule_labs[as.character(rule)], levels = rule_labs)]
if (nrow(d_info_all) > 0) {
  d_info_all[, rule_lab := factor(rule_labs[as.character(rule)], levels = rule_labs)]
}

n_interim <- max(d_dec_all$i_anlys)

# cumulative enrolment at each interim, taken from the first scenario's design
cum_enrol <- cumsum(cfg1$N)

# ---- 0. assumed true effects (risk-difference scale) ------------------------
table_truth <- function() {
  d <- dcast(d_truth_all, scenario ~ domain, value.var = "truth")
  d <- d[match(scenario_names, scenario)]
  setnames(d, c("scenario", paste0("d", 1:4)),
           c("Scenario", domain_labs_short[paste0("d", 1:4)]))
  d
}

# ---- 1. headline table: chance of each decision by the final interim --------
table_dec_final <- function() {
  d <- d_dec_all[i_anlys == n_interim]
  d[, rule_chr := factor(as.character(rule), levels = c("sup", "ni", "fut"))]
  d_w <- dcast(d, scenario ~ domain + rule_chr, value.var = "mu")
  d_w <- d_w[match(scenario_names, scenario)]
  setnames(d_w, "scenario", "Scenario")
  d_w
}

# ---- 2. progression by interim, one domain at a time ------------------------
plot_dec_domain <- function(dm, ncol = 3) {
  d <- d_dec_all[domain == dm]
  d[, scenario_lab := scn_factor(scenario)]

  d_lab <- merge(unique(d[, .(scenario, scenario_lab)]),
                 d_truth_all[domain == dm, .(scenario, truth)], by = "scenario")
  d_lab[, label := sprintf("True effect: %+.1f pp", truth * 100)]

  ggplot(d, aes(x = i_anlys, y = mu, colour = rule_lab, linetype = rule_lab)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    geom_text(data = d_lab, aes(x = Inf, y = 0.03, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.05, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
    facet_wrap(~ scenario_lab, ncol = ncol) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = rule_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n_interim)) +
    labs(x = "Interim analysis", y = "Cumulative chance of this decision",
         colour = "Decision", linetype = "Decision") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))
}

table_dec_domain <- function(dm) {
  d <- d_dec_all[domain == dm]
  d_w <- dcast(d, scenario + rule_lab ~ i_anlys, value.var = "mu")
  int_cols <- as.character(seq_len(n_interim))
  setnames(d_w, int_cols, paste("Interim", int_cols))
  d_w <- merge(d_w, d_truth_all[domain == dm, .(scenario, truth)], by = "scenario")
  d_w[, Scenario := sprintf("%s (true effect %+.1f pp)", scenario, truth * 100)]
  d_w[, scn_ord := match(scenario, scenario_names)]
  setorder(d_w, scn_ord, rule_lab)
  d_w[, Decision := as.character(rule_lab)]
  d_w[, c("scenario", "truth", "scn_ord", "rule_lab") := NULL]
  setcolorder(d_w, c("Scenario", "Decision"))
  d_w[]
}

# ---- 3. enrolment and patients informing each decision ----------------------
table_n_domain <- function(dm) {
  d <- d_info_all[domain == dm]
  d[, scn_ord := match(scenario, scenario_names)]
  setorder(d, scn_ord, rule_lab)
  d[, .(
    Scenario = scenario,
    Decision = as.character(rule_lab),
    `Chance of this decision` = pr_dec,
    `Enrolled at decision` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f to %.0f)", mu_n_enrl, q025_n_enrl, q975_n_enrl),
    `Informing the decision` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f to %.0f)", mu_n_info, q025_n_info, q975_n_info),
    `Share of enrolled informing` = prop_info
  )]
}
```

# Overall summary across scenarios

This section puts all scenarios side by side, so the behaviour of each comparison can be seen across the range of assumed truths.

## Assumed true effects

The true effects are the standardised risk differences implied by the sim07 data-generating process for the sim07 estimands, evaluated in the design population (all domains open, before any adaptation changes allocation).
They are shown in percentage points.
Because the sim07 and sim09 estimands differ (most notably for D1, where sim07 holds the downstream D2/D3 treatment at the 'not entered' level), a scenario with the same label can imply a different true effect in the two reports.

```{r table-truth}
d_truth_tbl <- table_truth()
gt(d_truth_tbl) |>
  fmt_number(columns = -Scenario, scale_by = 100, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_header(title = "Assumed true risk difference (pp) by domain") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 13)
```

## Chance of each decision

For each domain, the first decision reached locks that domain, so within a domain the possible decisions are mutually exclusive.
The remainder (100% less the decision columns) is the chance that the domain is still open at the final interim.
The first table gives the position at the final interim (interim `r n_interim`, cumulative enrolment of `r cum_enrol[n_interim]`).
The domain tabs that follow show how those chances build up over the interim analyses (cumulative enrolment at interims 1 to `r n_interim` is `r paste(cum_enrol, collapse = ", ")`).
The true effect for each scenario is on the risk-difference scale in percentage points (pp).

```{r table-dec-final}
d_final <- table_dec_final()
d_cols <- setdiff(names(d_final), "Scenario")

d_final_gt <- gt(d_final) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = d_cols, decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(.list = setNames(
    as.list(rule_labs[sub("^d[0-9]_", "", d_cols)]), d_cols)) |>
  tab_header(title = paste0("Chance of each decision by interim ", n_interim)) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 13)

# one spanner per domain
for (dm in unique(sub("_.*$", "", d_cols))) {
  d_final_gt <- tab_spanner(
    d_final_gt, label = domain_labs_short[[dm]],
    columns = grep(paste0("^", dm, "_"), d_cols, value = TRUE))
}
d_final_gt
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r overall-dec-domain, results='asis'}
for (dm in paste0("d", 1:4)) {

  cat("\n\n### ", domain_labs_short[dm], "\n\n")

  print(plot_dec_domain(dm))
  cat("\n\n")

  d_tbl <- table_dec_domain(dm)
  int_cols <- grep("^Interim", names(d_tbl), value = TRUE)
  print(
    gt(d_tbl, groupname_col = "Scenario") |>
      fmt_percent(columns = int_cols, decimals = 0) |>
      tab_options(table.font.size = 13)
  )
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

## Enrolment and patients informing each decision

These summaries describe the trials in which a decision was reached, at the interim where each domain's first decision occurred.
They should be read alongside the chance of the decision, because a decision that is rarely reached rests on very few simulated trials.

- **Enrolled at decision** is the total number of patients enrolled in the whole platform by that interim, not only those relevant to the domain.
  Decisions can only occur at an interim analysis, so this is one of the interim enrolment totals (`r paste(cum_enrol, collapse = ", ")`) and the average blends them.
- **Informing the decision** is the number of patients contributing to that domain's own comparison:
  D1 uses all patients in the late-acute group (DAIR, 1-stage and 2-stage revision), D2 uses 1-stage revision patients randomised to 12 or 6 weeks, D3 uses 2-stage revision patients randomised to 12 weeks or none, and D4 uses patients randomised to rifampicin or not.
- Ranges are the middle 95% across the simulated trials that reached that decision.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r overall-n-domain, results='asis'}
for (dm in paste0("d", 1:4)) {

  cat("\n\n### ", domain_labs_short[dm], "\n\n")

  d_tbl <- table_n_domain(dm)
  if (nrow(d_tbl) == 0) {
    cat("No decisions were reached for this domain in any scenario.\n\n")
    next
  }
  print(
    gt(d_tbl, groupname_col = "Scenario") |>
      fmt_percent(columns = c("Chance of this decision", "Share of enrolled informing"), decimals = 0) |>
      tab_options(table.font.size = 13)
  )
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::
